title: Start with requirements
hook: What must this system actually guarantee?
outcome: Turn a vague prompt into user flows, constraints and one measurable success criterion.
boundary: Separate functional requirements from latency, durability and availability targets.

title: Estimate traffic
hook: How many requests must this design handle?
outcome: Derive average and peak QPS from active users and operations per user.
boundary: State peak-factor assumptions; DAU is not concurrent users.

title: Estimate storage and bandwidth
hook: Will storage or bandwidth become the bottleneck?
outcome: Calculate bytes per day, retention, replication overhead and transfer rate using one worked example.
boundary: Label all quantities as assumptions; count indexes and replicas separately.

title: Latency, throughput and tail latency
hook: Why is the average fast while users still wait?
outcome: Separate response time from work completed per second; expose p99 and queueing as utilization rises.
boundary: Little’s Law uses steady-state average quantities; more concurrency can worsen overload.

title: Grow a simple architecture
hook: What breaks when one server becomes ten?
outcome: Evolve a client–app–database baseline with vertical scaling, horizontal scaling and externalized session state.
boundary: Add a component only for a named bottleneck; stateless app servers still depend on stateful systems.

title: DNS, TCP, TLS and connection reuse
hook: Why can the first request be slower?
outcome: Follow name lookup, connection setup and an HTTP exchange; show where reuse avoids work.
boundary: Latencies are illustrative; keep-alive and TLS resumption address different setup costs.

title: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3
hook: Can one lost packet stall several requests?
outcome: Show sequential responses, multiplexing and QUIC stream isolation with moving packets.
boundary: HTTP/2 still inherits TCP head-of-line blocking; QUIC has shared congestion control.

title: Reverse proxy, API gateway and load balancer
hook: Who handles this incoming request?
outcome: Map routing, TLS termination and application policies to the edge request path.
boundary: Roles overlap in products; explain responsibility rather than treating names as disjoint boxes.

title: Load balancing and health checks
hook: How do requests avoid an unhealthy server?
outcome: Compare round robin and least connections; eject a failed backend and maintain redundant ingress.
boundary: Health checks are imperfect; sticky sessions and unequal request costs change distribution.

title: CDNs and edge caching
hook: Why send every image across an ocean?
outcome: Trace edge hit versus origin miss and distinguish static, personalized and dynamic content.
boundary: Cache keys and freshness control correctness; DNS resolution and anycast routing are distinct mechanisms.

title: Choose storage from access patterns
hook: Which database does this workload need?
outcome: Choose among relational, key-value, document and wide-column models from queries and guarantees.
boundary: SQL/NoSQL labels do not determine consistency or transaction support.

title: Indexes and query access paths
hook: Why does a lookup scan a million rows?
outcome: Animate table scan versus index lookup; teach composite index order and covering queries.
boundary: Indexes add write and storage cost; column order must match predicates and sorting.

title: B+ trees and LSM trees
hook: Why can fast writes make later reads harder?
outcome: Follow page lookup versus buffered append, flush and compaction.
boundary: Read, write and space amplification depend on workload and configuration; avoid universal winners.

title: Transactions and durable commits
hook: What survives a crash halfway through a write?
outcome: Use a two-row money transfer to explain atomicity, commit and write-ahead logging.
boundary: Local ACID does not atomically include an external payment provider or message broker.

title: Normalization and denormalization
hook: Why store the same fact twice?
outcome: Compare joined source data with a read-optimized materialized view.
boundary: Denormalization creates an update and reconciliation obligation.

title: Object storage and large files
hook: Should the database store every video byte?
outcome: Separate metadata from blob bytes; trace a client upload using a scoped presigned URL.
boundary: An uploaded blob can exist before its metadata is finalized; validate and reconcile incomplete uploads.

title: Distributed identifiers
hook: How do servers create IDs without taking turns?
outcome: Compare random UUIDs, time-ordered UUIDs and Snowflake-style IDs against coordination and index locality.
boundary: Time order is not causal order; clocks, worker identity, collision risk and guessability matter.

title: Cache-aside reads
hook: Why ask the database for the same thing again?
outcome: Animate miss → database read → populate → hit; explain locality and bounded cache capacity.
boundary: A cache is usually a copy; design the miss and cache-down paths.

title: Cache writes and invalidation
hook: Why does a successful update show old data?
outcome: Trace a stale-value race; compare invalidate-on-write, write-through and write-back guarantees.
boundary: TTL bounds some staleness; it does not repair every race. Write-back needs explicit durability.

title: TTL and eviction
hook: Which cached item should leave first?
outcome: Separate expiry from capacity eviction; compare LRU, LFU and FIFO on the same request sequence.
boundary: Policy choice depends on access patterns; expiry and eviction are independent.

title: Sharding and shard keys
hook: Why is one database hot while others are idle?
outcome: Compare range and hash placement; choose a key from the dominant query and demonstrate a hotspot.
boundary: Cross-shard queries, secondary indexes and repartitioning have costs; table size alone is not a trigger.

title: Consistent hashing
hook: Why does adding one node move so much data?
outcome: Compare modulo remapping with a ring and virtual nodes.
boundary: Minimal expected movement assumes suitable key distribution; a hot key stays hot.

title: Replication, lag and failover
hook: Why does refresh hide a change you just saved?
outcome: Follow primary commit and asynchronous replica catch-up; show read routing for read-your-writes.
boundary: Replicas do not multiply write capacity or replace backups; failover can lose unreplicated writes.

title: Consistency models
hook: Which version is this read allowed to return?
outcome: Compare linearizability, eventual convergence and session guarantees with one write/read timeline.
boundary: Read-your-writes and monotonic reads are distinct; eventual consistency does not promise a fixed delay.

title: CAP and the normal-path trade-off
hook: What should a disconnected replica do?
outcome: Partition a replicated service; contrast refusal with potentially stale answers, then introduce PACELC.
boundary: CAP consistency means linearizability; availability is a formal response guarantee, not a general uptime score.

title: Quorums and consensus
hook: How can replicas agree on one decision?
outcome: Show majority log commitment and quorum intersection; distinguish voting from a consensus protocol.
boundary: R + W > N alone does not establish linearizability; membership, versions and failure assumptions matter.

title: Leases, distributed locks and fencing
hook: What if an old leader wakes up late?
outcome: Expire one worker’s lease and let a replacement take over; reject the stale worker with a fencing token.
boundary: A lease or lock alone cannot stop a paused worker’s later side effects.

title: Concurrency and isolation
hook: Can two customers buy the last seat?
outcome: Show lost update and check-then-write races; fix one invariant using conditional updates or locking.
boundary: Isolation levels have different anomalies; serializable transactions can require retries.

title: Distributed transactions and sagas
hook: What if payment succeeds but the order fails?
outcome: Compare coordinated commit with local steps and compensating actions using an order workflow.
boundary: Compensation is a business action and can fail; do not present a saga as an ACID rollback.

title: Work queues and retained event logs
hook: Why can two consumers need the same event?
outcome: Compare work distribution with a retained log and independent consumer positions.
boundary: Products can support several delivery modes; avoid equating a brand with one abstract model.

title: Acknowledgements and delivery guarantees
hook: Did the worker finish before it crashed?
outcome: Move a crash before and after the side effect and acknowledgement; expose loss versus duplicate execution.
boundary: Exactly-once claims need a stated transaction boundary; external effects need their own protection.

title: Partitions, ordering and consumer groups
hook: Why did event two arrive before event one?
outcome: Route related events to a partition; scale consumers while showing per-partition ordering.
boundary: Global ordering limits parallelism; ordering is not automatic across producers, partitions or retries.

title: Idempotency and safe retries
hook: Could one retry charge you twice?
outcome: Reuse one operation key; atomically claim, protect the effect and replay an appropriate result.
boundary: Scope keys, match payloads, retain records and propagate protection across external boundaries.

title: Transactional outbox and CDC
hook: What if the database commits but the event disappears?
outcome: Commit business state and an outbox row together; let a relay or CDC publish later.
boundary: Publishing can repeat; consumers still need deduplication and relevant ordering.

title: Poison messages, DLQs and replay
hook: Can one bad event stop the entire queue?
outcome: Bound retries, isolate a malformed message and reprocess it after repair.
boundary: DLQs need owners, monitoring and safe replay; moving an event can affect ordering.

title: Deadlines, retries and jitter
hook: Can retrying make an outage worse?
outcome: Propagate a deadline and disperse retries using backoff, jitter and a retry budget.
boundary: Retry only suitable failures and protected operations; layered retries can multiply traffic.

title: Backpressure and load shedding
hook: What if requests arrive faster than work finishes?
outcome: Fill a bounded queue; distinguish slowing producers, limiting concurrency and rejecting excess work.
boundary: An unbounded queue moves the outage into latency and memory; autoscaling takes time.

title: Rate limiting
hook: Should a client burst or send steadily?
outcome: Compare token bucket, leaky bucket and a sliding-window policy against a clear quota.
boundary: Distributed enforcement needs atomic decisions; per-user fairness and global limits differ.

title: Circuit breakers and bulkheads
hook: Can a broken dependency consume every worker?
outcome: Fail fast after repeated failures and isolate resource pools so unrelated work survives.
boundary: A breaker needs recovery probes; isolation and fallback have capacity and correctness trade-offs.

title: Cache stampedes and hot keys
hook: What happens when the popular key expires?
outcome: Contrast synchronized misses, jittered expiry, request coalescing and stale-while-revalidate.
boundary: Negative caching helps repeated misses; hot-key capacity and freshness need separate decisions.

title: Multi-region recovery and disaster recovery
hook: What survives when a region disappears?
outcome: Trace active-passive failover and separate replication, backups, RPO and RTO.
boundary: Active-active adds conflict resolution; recovery targets must be tested, not assumed.

title: Observability, SLOs and error budgets
hook: How do you know the system is healthy?
outcome: Tie request traces, metrics and logs to a user-visible latency or availability SLO.
boundary: Use tail latency, queue age and actionable alerts; a green process is not a healthy user journey.

title: Authentication, authorization and tenant isolation
hook: Can a logged-in user read someone else’s data?
outcome: Separate identity verification from per-resource permission checks; propagate tenant scope through storage and caches.
boundary: Tokens do not grant every permission; isolate cache keys and redact sensitive logs.

title: Monoliths, service boundaries and discovery
hook: Does this feature need a new service?
outcome: Choose boundaries by ownership, change patterns and independent scaling; show endpoint discovery after a split.
boundary: A service split adds network failure and operational cost; microservices are not a required milestone.

title: Safe releases and schema evolution
hook: Why did a harmless deploy break old clients?
outcome: Keep old and new versions compatible with expand–migrate–contract; use one canary and rollback example.
boundary: Queued events, old clients and replicas outlive a deploy; destructive changes need staged migration.

title: Cost, retention and data lifecycle
hook: What does this design cost every month?
outcome: Estimate storage, replicas, request volume and egress; select retention and tiering from product requirements.
boundary: Use assumed unit costs, not universal price claims; deletion must consider derived copies and backups.

title: Real-time updates
hook: Does the server need to push, or both sides talk?
outcome: Choose polling, SSE or WebSockets from direction and update frequency; show reconnect and missed-event recovery.
boundary: A live connection does not provide durable delivery; long polling is a variation, not a whole new architecture.

title: Feeds and fan-out
hook: Why is a celebrity different from a normal user?
outcome: Compare fan-out-on-write with fan-out-on-read and a hybrid for skewed follower counts.
boundary: Delivery, ranking and freshness are different concerns; materialized feeds need repair paths.

title: Search and autocomplete
hook: Why is search not just a database filter?
outcome: Build a derived inverted index; distinguish document retrieval from prefix suggestion lookup.
boundary: Indexes lag source data; typo tolerance and ranking are separate extensions.

title: Media processing and delivery
hook: What happens between Upload and Play?
outcome: Follow direct upload → queued transcoding → stored renditions → CDN → segment-based playback.
boundary: Processing states, failed jobs and bandwidth matter; protocol details stay outside the core reel.

title: Notifications and webhooks
hook: How does an event become one useful notification?
outcome: Trace a durable event through preferences, channel selection and a retrying delivery worker.
boundary: Deduplication, provider throttles, callback signatures and receipt status need explicit ownership.

title: Nearby queries and location updates
hook: How do you find nearby drivers efficiently?
outcome: Turn coordinates into spatial cells, query candidate neighborhoods and filter exact distance.
boundary: Cell boundaries and stale coordinates matter; matching and ETA are additional problems.

title: URL shortener — minimal working design
hook: Where does a short link come from?
outcome: State requirements and a worked traffic assumption; define create/redirect APIs, ID strategy and lookup storage.
boundary: Explain redirects and expiry; keep analytics off the critical redirect path.

title: URL shortener — scale and failures
hook: What if one short link becomes viral?
outcome: Evolve the same diagram with caching, sharding, abuse controls and redirect-path recovery.
boundary: Choose a shard key and identify the actual failure bottleneck; avoid repeating concept definitions.

title: Social feed — write and read paths
hook: Who builds the feed before you open it?
outcome: Define post/follow/feed access patterns and materialized timelines using previously taught fan-out.
boundary: Separate candidate delivery from ranking; show one practical cursor-pagination decision.

title: Social feed — celebrity spike and repair
hook: What happens when millions follow one author?
outcome: Switch high-fan-out authors to read-time merge; handle lag, duplicates and rebuild of derived feeds.
boundary: Keep stable cursor semantics and a source of truth for repair.

title: Chat — durable message delivery
hook: When is a message really sent?
outcome: Trace sender → durable append → receiver; define message IDs, conversation partitioning and acknowledgements.
boundary: Distinguish accepted, delivered and read; connection state is separate from message storage.

title: Chat — reconnects, ordering and duplicates
hook: What happens after the phone goes offline?
outcome: Resume from a cursor; deduplicate retried sends and recover connection routing after a node failure.
boundary: Explain per-conversation order and lag; presence can be eventually consistent.

title: Checkout — stock and payment invariants
hook: How do you sell the last item only once?
outcome: Define stock reservation and order state; protect inventory with a conditional update and payment with idempotency.
boundary: An invariant drives the architecture; payment, reservation and final order are distinct states.

title: Checkout — partial failure and recovery
hook: What if payment works but checkout times out?
outcome: Continue the same state machine with outbox events, compensation, retry handling and reconciliation.
boundary: Specify reservation expiry and refund failure handling; one timeout does not determine payment outcome.
